blocks.text: But there is no need to change anything, since all the books agree on the received reading, and it contains nothing at which a learned reader could rightly [col. 490] take offence. For it is certain that the eating of locusts was very widely accepted in the regions that lie either to the east or to the south. These are Jerome's words in Against Jovinian book 2, ch. 6: Among the peoples of the East and of Libya, because clouds of locusts are found throughout the desert and the vastness of the wilderness, it is the custom to feed on locusts. Thus, from the age of Alexander, Greece described among the peoples of Ethiopia the Acridophagi, so called from eating locusts. On these Agatharchides, book 5, ch. 27: Ὑπὸ δὲ τὴν ἐαριτὴν ἰσημερίαν, ὅτε Λίβυες (lege Λίβες) παρ᾽ αὐτοῖς καὶ Ζέφυροι πνέουσι, παμμεγεθῶν ἀκρίδων πλῆθος ἀμύθητον ἐκ τῆς ἀνιςορήτου μετὰ τῶν ἀνέμων παραγίνεται χώρας. τῇ μὲν δυνάμει τῆς πλήσεως τῶν ὀρνίθων μικρὸν παραλλάττον, [III, 329] μακρὸν δὲ τῷ σώματι. ἀπὸ τούτου δὲ τοῦ ζώου τρέφονται πάντα τὸν χρόνον, ἄλλως τε τούτοις καὶ τεταριχευμένοις χρώμενοι. [Hypo de tēn earitēn isēmerian, hote Libyes (lege Libes) par᾽ autois kai Zephyroi pneousi, pammegethōn akridōn plēthos amythēton ek tēs anistorētou meta tōn anemōn paraginetai chōras. tē men dynamei tēs plēseōs tōn ornithōn mikron parallatton, makron de tō sōmati. apo toutou de tou zōou trephontai panta ton chronon, allōs te toutois kai tetarichеumenois chrōmenoi.] Around the spring equinox, when the south-west winds and west winds blow among them, an indescribable swarm of very large locusts flies in together with the winds from unknown lands; in the force of their flight they differ little from birds, but in body very greatly. On this little creature they feed at every season, either salted or otherwise preserved. So also Diodorus, book 3 of Stephanus's edition, p. 113: Ἐκ τούτου δαψιλεῖς τροφὰς ἔχουσιν ἅπαντα τὸν βίον [Ek toutou dapsileis trophas echousin hapanta ton bion]: From it they have abundant sustenance throughout their whole life. And Artemidorus in Strabo, book 16: Ζῶσι δ' ἀπὸ ἀκρίδων, ἃς οἱ ἐαρινοὶ Λίβες καὶ Ζέφυροι, πνέοντες μεγάλοι, συνελαύνουσιν εἰς τοὺς τόπους τούτους· [Zōsi d' apo akridōn, has hoi earinoi Libes kai Zephyroi, pneontes megaloi, synelaunousin eis tous topous toutous] They live on locusts, which the spring south-west winds and west winds, blowing strongly, drive into those places. And Solinus: The neighbours of Mauretania at a certain season gather land locusts and, having hardened them in brine, keep them as their only means of subsistence. And Pliny, book 6, ch. 30: A certain part of the Ethiopians lives on locusts alone, hardened with smoke and salt as their yearly food. And book 11, ch. 29: among the Parthians these too are welcome as food. And on the Nasamones, Eustathius on Dionysius: Ἐσθίουσι δὲ ἀττελάβους πρὸς ἥλιον ξηράναντες· εἶδος δὲ ἀκρίδος ὁ ἀττέλαβος· [Esthiousi de attelabous pros hēlion xēranantes; eidos de akridos ho attelabos] They eat attelabi, a species of locust, dried in the sun. And Dioscorides, where he treats of the asiracus, a species of locust: Χρῶνται δ' αὐτῇ κατακόρως οἱ κατὰ Λέπτιν Λίβυες· [Chrōntai d' autē katakorōs hoi kata Leptin Libyes] The Libyans who live near Leptis use it as food to the point of satiety. Porphyry also, in book 1 of On Abstinence from Meat, writes that clouds of locusts presented themselves to an army suffering from hunger in Libya.

What of the fact that in Greece itself the same food was in use, which is easy to prove? In Aristophanes' Acharnians, Act 4, Scene 1, a Boeotian peasant, among the foods for sale that he brings to the market at Athens, says that he has something
Τῶν ὀρταλίχων, ἢ τῶν τετραπτερυλλίδων, [Tōn ortalichōn, ē tōn tetrapterullidōn,]
of hens, or of locusts, which, as we have observed ^{a)}, are called τετραπτερυλλίδας [tetrapterullidas] from the four wings with which they are furnished. And Scene 7:

Δ. Βούλει περιδόσθαι κἀπιτρέψαι Λαμάχῳ, Πότερον ἀκρίδες ἥδιόν ἐστιν, ἢ κίχλαι; Λ. Οἴμ' ὡς ὑβρίζεις. Δ. Τὰς ἀκρίδας κρίνει πολύ. [D. Boulei peridosthai kapitrepsai Lamachō, Poteron akrides hēdion estin, ē kichlai? L. Oim' hōs hybrizeis. D. Tas akridas krinei poly.]
